diseases.name: Downy Mildew
diseases.description: A water-mould disease of grapevine leaves, shoots and young berries.
diseases.causes: Warm, wet weather: rain splashes spores from the soil and leaf litter onto leaves, which must stay wet for hours to be infected.
symptoms: Yellow, oily-looking spots on the upper leaf
White downy growth under the spots in humid nights
Spots turn brown; young berries go grey and shrivel
diseases.effect: Infected leaves die and fall, and berry bunches can be lost.
diseases.untreated: Severe years strip vines of leaves, so fruit and wood ripen poorly.

steps.title: Remove infected leaves and clusters
steps.instruction: Take off spotted leaves and grey bunches and remove them.
steps.rationale: Each spot releases spores on humid nights.

steps.title: Open the canopy
steps.instruction: Thin shoots and remove leaves around the bunches.

steps.title: Protective fungicide before rain
steps.instruction: Spray a registered product on the label's schedule from early shoot growth.
steps.rationale: Protects new leaves; it cannot cure spots already there.

prevention.title: Clear fallen leaves
prevention.detail: The water mould overwinters in them.

prevention.title: Watch after warm rain in spring
prevention.detail: The first infections follow warm, wet spells.

lifecycle: Spores survive in leaf litter and soil.
Rain splashes them onto wet leaves.
Oily yellow spots appear, white down forms underneath.
New spores spread on wind and rain to leaves and berries.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: grape downy mildew

diseases.name: Grapevine Leafroll
diseases.description: A virus disease of grapevines that reddens and rolls the leaves in late summer and spoils the fruit.
diseases.causes: Spread in infected cuttings and rootstocks, and from vine to vine by mealybugs and soft scale insects.
symptoms: Red to purple leaves between green main veins (red varieties)
Yellowing instead of red on white varieties
diseases.effect: Grapes ripen late with less sugar and poor colour.
diseases.untreated: Infected vines stay infected; yield and quality fall over the years and the disease spreads along the row.

steps.title: Mark the vine
steps.instruction: Flag vines with symptoms in late summer.
steps.rationale: Symptoms are clearest then; marked vines can be removed later.

steps.title: Control mealybugs
steps.instruction: Check for mealybugs and treat as advised locally.
steps.rationale: Mealybugs carry the virus from vine to vine.

steps.title: Remove infected vines
steps.instruction: Pull out infected vines and replant with certified stock.
steps.rationale: There is no cure; removal stops the spread.

prevention.title: Plant certified virus-tested vines
prevention.detail: Most new outbreaks start from infected nursery stock.

lifecycle: The virus is in the vine's sap.
Mealybugs feeding on it pick it up.
They carry it to nearby vines; cuttings carry it farther.
Leaves redden and roll from late summer.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: grapevine leafroll disease
